purpose: This is the cryptographic/verification core of the Hookemon 'cycle' engine (one buy-pack -> open -> sell-back -> return-proceeds pass). None of the 10 src files under review implement real network calls; every function is prefixed 'fixture' and verifies pre-signed JSON evidence objects using hardcoded Ed25519 test keys, standing in for what production Collector Crypt / Solana RPC / owner-signing / accounting-oracle integrations must eventually verify. Each file exposes an explicit verifyProductionX() stub that throws Error('INTEGRATION_PENDING: ...') -- production verification is not implemented anywhere in this file set. One file (vault-payout-authorization.mjs) is the exception: it implements real, non-fixture cryptography (Solidity abi.encode-compatible field packing + a from-scratch Keccak-256) that would be used identically in fixture and production, because it just prepares the digest an on-chain vault contract must recompute.

files.role: Two pure validators: validateCycleCustody() enforces custody role separation (returnAccount===cycleVaultAccount; operationsTrigger, the 20-minute cron trigger, can never equal cycleVaultAccount or policyAccount, i.e. automation cannot custody funds; cycleVaultAccount!==policyAccount). validateBinding() enforces the exact one-pack binding schema: sourceChainId===4663 (Robinhood Chain), executionCluster==='mainnet-beta' (hardcoded to real Solana mainnet, no devnet/testnet path), circleDollarMint fixed to Circle's real Circle USD-mainnet mint 'EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v' with 6 decimals, pack==='collector-crypt' hardcoded, quantity===1 hardcoded, turbo===false hardcoded, refundTokenAccountOwner===executionWallet (self-custody only).

Fixture-only transaction message codec: builds/validates a JSON envelope ('hookemon.fixture-message.v1') standing in for a decoded Solana transaction (instructions, accounts, signers, validity window, binding), encodes it to canonical hex, decodes with strict canonical-round-trip checking, and verifies a signed-transaction envelope ('hookemon.fixture-signed-transaction.v1') against exactly the required signer set derived from the message's `signers` array. Only one signer role key is registered (fixture-fee-payer) -- true multi-signer transactions are unmodeled. verifyProductionTransaction() throws INTEGRATION_PENDING.

Gate that must be recorded before ANY external intent for a cycle. At module load time it reads architecture/interfaces.json and hard-asserts schemaVersion, productPhase===1, requirementsRevision===56, architectureRevision===4, and status==='FROZEN_BUILD_CONTRACT_PRODUCTION_INTEGRATION_PENDING' -- import throws if these drift. verifyFixtureCyclePreflight() cross-checks an owner-signed spend plan against an independently-signed on-chain 'release' evidence object (chainId hardcoded '4663', asset 'USDG'), requires totalPrincipal===releasedAmount<=spendCap (no partial spend, no over-cap), requires 4 distinct nonzero EVM addresses (operationsTrigger/cycleVaultAccount/hook/usdg), and requires bindingManifestDigest to equal the frozen FIXTURE_BINDING_MANIFEST_DIGEST.

Owner-approval digesting/verification plus a lightweight in-memory AuthorizationLedger. Two approval domains: general owner approval ('hookemon.fixture-owner-approval.v1', kinds mutation/sign/broadcast/asset-spend/gas-spend) and a distinct post-open buyback approval domain used only after the Collector card is revealed (can't be pre-authorized because the drawn card is unknown in advance). All expiry checks compare against a single frozen constant FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_VALIDATED_AT='2029-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', not wall-clock time -- fixtureAuthorizationStoreRecord() explicitly refuses any other validatedAt ('validation time is not trusted').

Real (non-fixture) production code: encodeVaultPayoutAuthorization() packs a 16-field tuple (requirementsRevision, chainId, cycleId, hook, vault, usdg, operationsTrigger, bindingManifestDigest, payoutId, manifestDigest, rootHash, rootSum, returnActionDigest, returnReceiptDigest, expiresAt, nonce) exactly as Solidity abi.encode(uint256...) would, and keccak256() is a from-scratch Keccak-f[1600]/rate-136 implementation (correct 0x01/0x80 padding, distinct from NIST SHA3's 0x06). vaultPayoutAuthorizationDigest() = keccak256(encode(...)) is what an on-chain vault contract would need to recompute to accept a payout claim.

Verifies every Collector Crypt interaction as a discrete signed evidence object: generate/open request+digest, owner mutation authorization (binds wallet to both binding.executionWallet and the request, requires prizeWallet==='fixture-destination-purchase' for generate), signed open-execution broadcast, provider-signed 'ready' status, provider-signed finalized open-custody (hard-enforces prePackBalance-postPackBalance===1n and postNftBalance-preNftBalance===1n, i.e. exactly one pack debited / one NFT credited), and RPC-signed finality binding back to the custody record. verifyProductionCollectorIntegration() throws INTEGRATION_PENDING.

Verifies an RPC-signed 'this blockhash is/was live' attestation: finalized===true, observedHeight<lastValidHeight (BigInt), signed by the same rpcPublicKey used for Collector RPC finality. Callers (cycle-runner.mjs, not in this unit) enforce it must be the most recently recorded validity immediately before broadcast.

The balance-delta reconciliation gate for every finalized action (outbound/purchase/buyback/return). verifyNativeGas() requires preBalance-postBalance===actualDebit===transactionFee exactly. verifyAccountActivity() requires a finalized, non-empty, in-window movement list per side, matching asset. verifyFixtureExecutionAccounting() requires source/destination(/NFT-destination for buyback) activity windows to all close on the SAME toBlockHeight/toBlockHash as the top-level evidence, and structurally mandates nftDestinationActivity only for actionKind==='buyback' before generic shape validation runs.

Optimistic-concurrency (begin/commit with baseVersion staleness check) dedup registry keyed by digest(provider, providerReceiptId): rejects a different record replacing an already-claimed provider receipt id, but tolerates idempotent re-consumption of the exact same record.

Standalone executable script (also imported by its own test): builds a CycleRunner+FixtureCycleStore, runs a full fixture cycle via executeCompleteFixtureCycle() imported FROM THE TEST DIRECTORY (../../test/cycle/fixture-cycle.mjs), closes it, serializes/reopens the store, recovers via CycleRunner.recover(), and asserts the recovered state matches (stage='closed', version=6) and the reopened snapshot is byte-identical.

Schemas referenced (defined in schemas.mjs, not in this unit): FIXTURE_ACTION_KINDS=['outbound','purchase','buyback','return'], FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_KINDS=['mutation','sign','broadcast','asset-spend','gas-spend']
invariants: Operations trigger (the automated 20-minute cron caller) can never equal cycleVaultAccount or policyAccount -- automation is a trigger only, never a funds custodian (bindings.mjs validateCycleCustody).
returnAccount must equal cycleVaultAccount -- funds always return to the exact vault they left (bindings.mjs).
Every cycle spends its ENTIRE released amount, no more, no less: totalPrincipal===releasedAmount<=spendCap (preflight.mjs).

bindingManifestDigest must match the single frozen FIXTURE_BINDING_MANIFEST_DIGEST sourced from architecture/interfaces.json at module-load time; module import itself fails if requirementsRevision!==56 or architectureRevision!==4.
Exactly one pack per cycle: binding.quantity===1, binding.turbo===false, binding.pack==='collector-crypt' are all hardcoded equality checks, not configurable minimums/defaults.
Collector open custody must show exactly prePackBalance-postPackBalance===1 and postNftBalance-preNftBalance===1 (collector.mjs).
Native gas debit must exactly equal the independently verified transaction fee (execution-accounting.mjs verifyNativeGas): preBalance-postBalance===actualDebit===transactionFee.

Every activity window (source/destination/NFT-destination) in execution accounting must close on the identical toBlockHeight/toBlockHash as the top-level finalized evidence -- no mixing of stale sub-evidence with a fresh top-level claim.
A buyback action structurally requires nftDestinationActivity before generic shape checks run (accountingPayload chooses the field list by actionKind first).

Owner-approval expiry is checked only against the frozen constant FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_VALIDATED_AT, never real wall-clock time; fixtureAuthorizationStoreRecord() actively refuses any other validatedAt value.
Receipt registry: same (provider, providerReceiptId) key can be idempotently re-consumed only if the new record canonically equals the existing one; any divergent record is rejected outright.

AuthorizationLedger.consume() rejects a valid signature whose canonical payload differs from the caller's `expected` value (defends against 'same nonce, different terms' substitution) and rejects reuse of a consumed digest.

decodeFixtureOnlyMessage/verifyFixtureSignedTransaction check RECOVERY_LIMITS byte-length caps (messageHexChars/signedHexChars) BEFORE attempting hex-decode or JSON.parse -- DoS-input bound is checked first.

execution-accounting's verifyAccountActivity reads the raw property descriptor for `movements` (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor) before generic shape assertion, so a length-limit check never triggers a malicious getter early.
stateTransitions: No local FSM lives in these 10 files (the state machine itself is in cycle-runner.mjs, outside this unit's scope). These files are pure verify/encode functions consumed by the runner at specific transition points inferred from tests: recordReleasedCyclePreflight -> prepareExternalIntent -> recordOwnerAuthorization('mutation') -> consumeAuthorizationOnce -> executeAuthorizedExternalMutationOnce -> recordFixtureDecodedTransaction -> recordOwnerAuthorization('sign') -> recordSignedBytes -> recordOwnerAuthorization('broadcast'/'asset-spend'/'gas-spend') -> recordFixtureBlockhashValidity -> broadcastPreparedTransactionOnce -> appendCanonicalReceipt -> recordExecutionAccountingEvidence -> consumeReceiptOnce -> reconcileUnresolvedIntent -> advanceCycleState.

Collector-specific path: prepareCollectorGenerateIntent/prepareCollectorOpenIntent -> consumeCollectorMutationAuthorization -> executeAuthorizedExternalMutationOnce -> generateCollectorPack / openCollectorPack -> recordVerifiedCollectorStatus (required before open) -> recordFinalizedCollectorOpenCustody (requires independent RPC finality bound to the exact custody record) -> deriveOpenReconciliation.

Buyback specifically requires a distinct 'post-open' owner authorization domain (recordPostOpenBuybackAuthorization) that cannot be pre-issued during the generic mutation-approval flow -- a generic 'mutation' approval targeted at a buyback action is explicitly rejected ('post-open buyback' error observed in security.test.mjs).

Cycle-level closure (deriveClosedCycle) requires: continuous ledger balances end-to-end, Collector-open finality strictly before buyback finalization ('Collector open ... buyback chronology'), buyback refund exactly matching the post-open approval amount, and every appended receipt fully consumed (no dangling verified-but-unconsumed receipts).

consumeReturnedProceedsOnce -> preparePayoutFunding is gated on 'recorded distribution verification' evidence not present in this file set; vault-payout-authorization.mjs supplies only the ABI-encoding/hash primitive consumed at that step, not the verification gate itself.

architecture/interfaces.json (repo root) is a hard load-time dependency for preflight.mjs; a schemaVersion/productPhase/requirementsRevision/architectureRevision/status mismatch throws at import, not at call time
testStatus: All 75 tests across the 8 *.test.mjs files in packages/runner/test/cycle/ were executed directly with `node --test packages/runner/test/cycle/*.test.mjs` (Node v24.19.0) during this review and PASSED (75 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, ~13.3s wall time). No test is marked todo/skip. fixture-crypto.mjs and fixture-cycle.mjs are non-test helper modules (no 'test(' calls) shared by collector-sequence.test.mjs and security.test.mjs. verify-fixtures.test.mjs additionally execFileSync-runs verify-fixtures.mjs as a subprocess and asserts its stdout; that also passed. Nothing here is compile-only or disabled. Coverage is deep for the fixture/verification logic itself but there is zero coverage of the real production path, because that path (verifyProductionX functions) is not implemented -- those functions are only tested for throwing INTEGRATION_PENDING (runner.test.mjs, bindings-state-machine.test.mjs).
autonomyGaps: No production verification exists anywhere in this unit: collector.mjs.verifyProductionCollectorIntegration(), decoder.mjs.verifyProductionTransaction() both unconditionally throw INTEGRATION_PENDING. Unattended 20-minute cycles cannot run against real Collector Crypt / real Solana RPC until these are implemented and until an equivalent production preflight/authorization/accounting/blockhash-validity path exists (only fixture-signed paths exist today).

All owner-approval and Collector-mutation-authorization schemas require a synchronous Ed25519 signature from a human/HSM-held owner key for every phase (mutation, sign, broadcast, asset-spend, gas-spend, plus a separate post-open buyback approval) on every single action, and every Collector generate/open request. A dashboard-driven fully autonomous 20-minute loop needs either (a) a hot signing service holding the owner key and mechanically producing these approvals per policy, or (b) a redesigned schema that allows pre-authorizing a batch/policy rather than one signature per phase per action -- neither exists in this unit, and no code here even sketches how the owner key would be operated unattended.

quantity===1, pack==='collector-crypt', turbo===false are hardcoded equality checks in bindings.mjs -- the owner's dashboard requirement to 'choose which packs to buy' and vary quantity is not representable by the current binding schema without a schema and every downstream verifier rewrite.

The interval/dashboard/restart-stuck-cycle control plane described in the owner target has no corresponding code in this unit at all -- this file set is purely the cryptographic verification kernel for one action's evidence, not a scheduler.

FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_VALIDATED_AT is a frozen constant date (2029-01-01), not real time; there is no live wall-clock expiry function in this file set, so whatever replaces this for production must add real-time expiry checking from scratch.

The USDG(Robinhood Chain)<->Circle USD(Solana mainnet-beta) bridge step that must exist for 'buy a pack with process budget' and 'proceeds return to Robinhood USDG' is completely unmodeled here -- decoder.mjs only handles Solana-shaped instructions, preflight.mjs only handles the EVM-side release; nothing in this unit verifies a bridge transaction. (The historical mainnet-cycle-canary branch reportedly has a Relay bridge client, but it is out of scope/non-authoritative.)
decoder.mjs's fixtureSignerKeys Map has exactly one entry ('fixture-fee-payer') -- any production signer topology beyond a single fee-payer signer is unimplemented.

verify-fixtures.mjs (src/) importing executeCompleteFixtureCycle from test/cycle/fixture-cycle.mjs means the production source tree depends on test fixtures to even be importable/runnable; this is fragile for any packaging/build step that excludes test/ from what ships.

suspicions.note: Regex built via `new RegExp("^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}" + String.fromCharCode(36))` instead of the plain literal `/^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$/` used everywhere else in the same file and codebase. String.fromCharCode(36) is just '$'. No behavioral difference, but this is the only regex in the entire reviewed unit built this way -- looks like an artifact of a scripted edit or an attempt to dodge a secret/pattern scanner. Worth a git-blame check.

Defines its own private, non-exported `fixtureAuthorizationValidatedAt = '2029-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'` duplicating authorization.mjs's exported `FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_VALIDATED_AT` constant verbatim instead of importing it. If these two frozen-time constants are ever edited independently, Collector-authorization expiry and general-action-authorization expiry could silently diverge.

Production script under src/cycle imports `executeCompleteFixtureCycle` from `../../test/cycle/fixture-cycle.mjs` -- src depends on test/. security.test.mjs (line ~127-136) already has a guard test asserting the source text mentions CycleRunner/FixtureCycleStore.reopen and not a legacy state-machine, but nothing guards against this test-directory import breaking if test/cycle/fixture-cycle.mjs is refactored for test-only concerns.

The from-scratch Keccak-256 implementation is validated by exactly one test vector in vault-payout-authorization.test.mjs (a single fixed 16-field tuple hashing to a hardcoded expected digest). For a from-scratch cryptographic primitive whose correctness gates real on-chain payout authorization, one vector (no official Keccak/SHA3 test-vector suite, no multi-rate-block input, no empty-input case) is thin verification coverage even though the observed test passes.

Module-load-time hard assertion on architecture/interfaces.json's requirementsRevision===56 and architectureRevision===4 means this file (and everything importing it, including the whole cycle-runner) becomes UNIMPORTABLE the moment that JSON is bumped without a matching source edit -- consistent with the repo-wide 'STATE.md regenerates as STALE' issue already flagged for this repo; this is the concrete mechanism by which a policy.json/interfaces.json revision bump can hard-break module loading, not just soft-fail a status check.

circleDollarMint is hardcoded to Circle's real Solana mainnet Circle USD mint address, but the binding schema calls it 'circleDollarMint'/'circleDollarDecimals' rather than 'circle-usd' -- combined with executionCluster hardcoded to 'mainnet-beta', any test or fixture code path that constructs a binding object is nominally pointed at real mainnet Circle USD; nothing in this unit prevents a binding object built with this mint from being fed toward a live wallet if the runner is ever pointed at production RPC endpoints, since the fixture/production boundary lives in decoder.mjs and collector.mjs, not in bindings.mjs itself.

keyFacts: requirementsRevision hardcoded/enforced === 56 across preflight.mjs, vault-payout-authorization.mjs, and (per grep) architecture/interfaces.json; architectureRevision===4 enforced only in preflight.mjs's module-load guard.

chainId '4663' (decimal string) = Robinhood Chain, asserted in preflight.mjs's releaseEvidence check and validateVaultPayoutAuthorization's readUint bound check; binding.sourceChainId===4663 (number) in bindings.mjs.
binding.executionCluster fixed to 'mainnet-beta' (real Solana mainnet, no devnet path in this schema).
Circle Circle USD mainnet mint on Solana hardcoded: EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, 6 decimals.

4 distinct hardcoded Ed25519 public keys embedded as raw DER-SPKI hex across this unit: owner (70b70676...ca34ca), transaction-signer/fee-payer (82479392...49dbc0ca23f7), provider (0378aa0d...1dddfd1), rpc (d64a93ba...cd619f03). A 5th, distinct 'accounting' public key (70dbd84e...b593a2f1) is defined separately in execution-accounting.mjs, and a 6th distinct 'release' public key (71baabb4...4bdd6a1a96b93) is defined separately in preflight.mjs -- 6 total fixture authority keys across the unit, all literal source constants.

FIXTURE_ACTION_KINDS = ['outbound','purchase','buyback','return']; FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_KINDS = ['mutation','sign','broadcast','asset-spend','gas-spend'] (both defined in schemas.mjs, confirmed via grep, consumed throughout this unit).
FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_VALIDATED_AT = '2029-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', used as the sole 'current time' for every expiry check in the fixture layer.
Collector custody invariant: prePackBalance-postPackBalance===1n and postNftBalance-preNftBalance===1n (exactly one pack for exactly one NFT, always).
Preflight requires totalPrincipal===releasedAmount<=spendCap -- no partial spend of a released cycle.

vaultPayoutAuthorizationDigest test vector: input tuple in vault-payout-authorization.test.mjs hashes to 0xbef14401bf2d1ac58835943567d23df458ddc323612e0f63c5e8d4bffafc523a, confirmed by direct byte count to be exactly 32 bytes (64 hex chars after 0x) -- a correctly-sized keccak256 output, and the test passes under node --test.
All 10 src files total 995 lines; all 10 test files total 3093 lines (security.test.mjs alone is 2002 lines, 2x the combined src line count).
Test run: 75/75 node:test cases pass under Node v24.19.0 via `node --test packages/runner/test/cycle/*.test.mjs`.
openQuestions: Where does the 6-fixture-key trust model (owner, transaction-signer, provider, rpc, accounting, release) map to production key custody? Is there a plan for who/what holds and operates the 'owner' Ed25519 key in an unattended 20-minute-cycle production deployment, given every phase (mutation/sign/broadcast/asset-spend/gas-spend, plus post-open buyback) requires a fresh owner signature per action per cycle?

How will the dashboard's 'choose which packs to buy' and adjustable interval/quantity features be reconciled with bindings.mjs's hardcoded pack==='collector-crypt', quantity===1, turbo===false equality checks -- is a Phase-2 schema revision (e.g. the unmerged codex/phase2-revision-57 line) expected to replace this file, and if so does it preserve the custody-separation and one-pack-per-custody-credit invariants this unit currently enforces?

Does the USDG(Robinhood)<->Circle USD(Solana) bridge verification exist anywhere in the current mainline, or is it entirely absent pending the historical mainnet-cycle-canary branch's Relay bridge client being ported in? This unit gives no evidence either way.

Is the src->test import in verify-fixtures.mjs (importing test/cycle/fixture-cycle.mjs from src/cycle/verify-fixtures.mjs) intentional/permanent, or should fixture-cycle.mjs be relocated so src/ has no test/ dependency for packaging purposes?
